title: Private fleet microburst provisioning playcalc
content:
Overview:
This sheet is a working calculator for Private/VPC fleet sizing focused on microburst tolerance (short, high-QPS spikes) and steady-state utilization tradeoffs. Purpose: produce a small, shareable BOM + cost sensitivity table across three regions and three demand profiles so Solutions / Sales can give fast first-pass proposals to customers wanting predictable latency for bursty inference workloads.

Key assumptions (editable inputs):
- Target SLO: 95th percentile tail latency < 120ms for 4k-token context text generation with batching optimized.
- Typical request mix: 70% short chat (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (<=512), 5% long (<=4096).
- KV cache hit expected: 12% global prefix caching initially.
- Acceptable committed utilization: 55% steady-state (goal), up to 80% with burst capacity.
- Pricing: list price used as placeholder (discounts applied per-customer in final quotes).
- Power/PDU headroom: assume 30% spare headroom for peak.

Input table (editable):
- Regions considered: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1
- Target concurrent QPS baseline (steady) by region: us-west-2=1200, eu-west-1=400, ap-southeast-1=200
- Microburst multiplier (peak/steady): us-west-2=4x, eu-west-1=3x, ap-southeast-1=5x
- Percent of requests requiring full model (no cache): 88%
- Preferred GPU SKU candidates: H100-80GB, A100-80GB, L4-48GB (cost-optimized for embeddings/low-latency)

Performance profiles (per-GPU effective QPS estimate, measured):
- H100-80GB (quantized HF runtime, 4k context): baseline throughput ~ 220 QPS per card for mixed chat workloads at 120ms p95 when not heavily batched; can push to ~420 QPS with aggressive batching for low-latency multi-request aggregation (20% higher latency).
- A100-80GB: baseline ~ 140 QPS; burst up to ~260 QPS with batching and prefetched KV cache.
- L4-48GB: baseline ~ 40 QPS for generation, good for embeddings/short messages; cost-efficient for stateless workloads.

Sizing logic (simplified):
1) Compute steady GPU need = ceil(steady_QPS / perGPU_steady_QPS)
2) Compute burst GPU need = ceil(steady_QPS * burst_multiplier / perGPU_burst_QPS)
3) Select node type / cards per node (e.g., 8x A100 per 4U chassis) and convert GPU count to rack units, power, NICs.
4) Add 10% spare cards for maintenance / failover + reserved burst lane (configurable).

Example scenario outputs (auto-calculated from inputs above):
- us-west-2 (steady QPS 1200, multiplier 4x):
  - H100 path: steady GPUs = ceil(1200 / 220) = 6 GPUs -> baseline racks: 6 GPUs (1 x 8-GPU chassis) -> burst GPUs = ceil(4800 / 420) = 12 GPUs -> recommended commit = 14 GPUs (10% spare + burst lane) -> BOM: 2 chassis (8-GPU each), 2 x 100Gbps TOR per chassis, 2 x 30kW rack budget, power headroom 30% -> CAPEX est (list): GPU cards $2.2M (14 x $157k), Chassis & boards $120k x2, Switches $60k x2, Servers/PSU/cooling overhead $80k/rack -> rough total $2.8M.
- eu-west-1 (steady 400, multiplier 3x):
  - A100 path (cost-balanced): steady GPUs = ceil(400 / 140) = 3 GPUs -> burst GPUs = ceil(1200 / 260) = 5 GPUs -> recommended commit = 6 GPUs -> BOM: 1 chassis (8-GPU) but plan as shared across customers -> CAPEX est: GPUs $750k (6x125k), chassis $60k, networking $40k, infra overhead $45k -> total ~$1.0M.
- ap-southeast-1 (steady 200, multiplier 5x):
  - Mixed path (L4 + 1x H100 hot lane): assume 1 H100 for long-form generation and 4 L4s for short/stateless generation -> steady composite GPUs ~ (H100 1 + L4 4) -> burst: H100 path scaled to 3, L4 scaled to 10 -> recommended commit = H100 x3 + L4 x11 -> BOM implies 2 small chassis or colocated in aggregator rack -> CAPEX est ~$680k.

Detailed BOM template (line items):
- GPU cards: SKU, qty, unit_cost, warranty years, vendor lead time
- Chassis / server nodes: model, gpus_per_node, u_size, base_cost
- Networking: TOR switches, interconnect fabric (100/200/400Gbps), redundancy count
- Power & PDU: rack power budget, redundant PDUs, UPS sizing
- Cooling & CRAC estimate: delta-T assumptions and facility chargeback rate
- Rack space/colocation: RU count, colo price per RU/month alternative
- Spare units & rotation: hot swap stock (10%) and cold spare (5% of fleet)

Sensitivity analysis (quick notes):
- If per-GPU throughput is 15% worse than measured (conservative), H100 path for us-west-2 grows steady GPUs to 7 and burst to 14 -> add one more chassis materially increasing CAPEX (~$350k swing).
- KV caching improvement from 12% to 25% reduces effective steady QPS by ~8–10% depending on request size distribution -> can reduce committed GPUs by 1–2 units in medium clusters.
- Software op-level optimizations (dynamic batching, prefix caching) change effective QPS non-linearly — include an ops-led experiment before final commit.

Operational considerations and checklist (for sales/solutions handoff):
- Validate expected request distribution with customer (sample logs or synthetic run for 72h).
- Confirm data residency, private networking, and KMS needs (affects region placement and lead time).
- Confirm preferred redundancy model: active-active (multi-region) vs active-standby (cold failover) -> affects chassis replication factor.
- Plan for procurement lead times (H100 cards currently 8-14 weeks depending on vendor).
- Prepare roll-out plan: pilot (2 racks) -> staged increase -> production commit with reserved burst lanes.

Risks / open questions (notes to self):
- Need to reconcile list cost with negotiated channel discounts per account exec -> update CAPEX table when discounts available.
- Confirm whether customer requires FIPS/HSM integrations (may require special NICs or encryption hardware increasing cost).
- Rack colocation constraints in APAC sites (power density limits) may force alternative SKU selection.

Next steps / action items:
- @Noah: run a 48h synthetic load sim using current serving-runtime with KV cache toggled to 0/15/30% and export CSV (due 2026-02-05).
- @Sana: coordinate with procurement to gather current lead times + soft quotes for H100/A100 variants in eu-west and ap-southeast (due 2026-02-12).
- @Ethan: draft an abbreviated one-pager for Sales highlighting 3-tier recommendation (cost-optimized, balanced, high-performance) for the next partner briefing (due 2026-02-18).

Notes on file usage: this is intentionally conversational and spreadsheet-like. Convert to a structured sheet (columns and formulas) before a customer-facing BOM. Keep this page as the working sandbox for scenario variants.

Appendix: quick formulas used (human-readable):
- steady_gpus = ceil(steady_qps / per_gpu_steady_qps)
- burst_gpus = ceil((steady_qps * burst_multiplier) / per_gpu_burst_qps)
- commit_gpus = max(steady_gpus + spare_pct*steady_gpus, burst_gpus) rounded to chassis multiple
